tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

¬ HasRight (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).1 .modify 2 ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsG2).s
      (.ok ((run K0 [] opsG2).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1]))) ∧
    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsG2).s.A.length 2
      ((run K0 [] opsG2).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1])) .reject :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (ar := arD) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide,
    .ok (by decide), .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- **Init** (sequence accepting more than `issue`): the destination 2 is written (`write3`) before
the emission. The restricted `issue` of `[1]` into 2 is rejected by clause 2 (§77.2, "non `Init`");
`split` then `store` of the block into 2 are `ok` (O8.2: "Le fait que ses données soient déjà `Init`
n'interdit pas à lui seul l'opération"). -/
def opsInit : List Op := opsArena ++ [.write 2 [2]]

theorem ce_init :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsInit).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsInit).s.arenas = [arD] ∧
    IssueR arD [1] 2 (run K0 [] opsInit).s .reject ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsInit).s
      (.ok ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))) ∧
    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsInit).s.A.length 2
      ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))
      (.ok (storeEff ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))
        (run K0 [] opsInit).s.A.length 2)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide), .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- The entry of `opsAvail` once `[1]` is issued (block 5) and the block released. -/
def arDu : Arena := ⟨1, 4, [], [([1], 5)]⟩

/-- **Availability** (the role of the metadata, §77.4): after the emission of `[1]` into 2 and the
release of the block, `internal` has its effective `Modify` on 1 again but the region is still
issued. The restricted `issue` of `[1]` into 3 fails; `split` then `store` into 3 are `ok`. -/
def opsAvail : List Op := opsArena ++ [.issue 0 0 [1] 2, .release 5]

theorem ce_avail :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsAvail).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.arenas = [arDu] ∧
    IssueR arDu [1] 3 (run K0 [] opsAvail).s (.fail (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu) ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsAvail).s

    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.A.length 3

      (.ok (storeEff ((run K0 [] opsAvail).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu [1]))
        (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.A.length 3)) :=

/-- **Empty region**: the restricted `issue` of the empty region is `ok`; no place has an empty
footprint (`exists_mem_footprint`), so `derive` (O1), which takes a place, cannot produce the block,

  have hw := (reachable_invariants (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (reach_run (os := opsArena) (by decide))).1
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hw ((run K0 [] opsArena).s.P.length - q + 1) q (by omega) hq
  rw [he] at hl; simp at hl

value 0 by `store` (O8), which adds it to `D 0`. The restricted `reset` and the kernel `reset` are
rejected by their clause 3 (§78.3, the kernel reading `internal` within its subtree of origins) for
as long as 0 is usable; `derive` of `internal` on the storage then `release` are `ok`. -/
theorem ce_reset_anchor :

    ¬ ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsArena).s arD ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (run K0 [] opsArena).s .reject ∧

      (.ok (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify)) ∧
    ReleaseStep (run K0 [] opsArena).s.A.length (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify)
      (.ok (releaseEff (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify) (run K0 [] opsArena).s.A.length)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- An arena value that holds `internal` through `store` blocks the restricted `reset` while it is
usable. -/
theorem reset_blocked_by_stored_internal {s : S3} {ar : Arena} {v : Nat} (hv : s.Usable v)
    (hx : ar.internal ∈ s.D v) : ¬ ResetPreR s ar :=
  fun h => (h.2.2 v (List.mem_range.2 hv.lt) hv _ hx).1 rfl

/-- Prefix with an allocated storage: frame 1 with the leaves 0 (arena value), 1 (allocator
value), 2 and 3 (destinations); `alloc` of the storage 4, of parts 5 and 6, owned by 0, of root
authority 4 held by 0; `newArena 4 4`. `internal` is a root, in no `D`. -/
def opsAlloc : List Op :=
  [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1],
    .alloc 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)], .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4]

/-- The entry registered by `opsAlloc`. -/
def arL : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩

/-- **Empty derivation** (`reset`): `split` of `internal` on the empty region creates an active
derivation of empty footprint. The restricted `reset` and the kernel `reset` are rejected by their
clause 2 (§78.2); `derive` of `internal` on the storage then `release` are `ok`. -/
def opsEmpty : List Op := opsAlloc ++ [.split 4 [[]]]

theorem ce_reset_empty :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.arenas = [arL] ∧
    ¬ ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s arL ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 4 4 .modify (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s
      (.ok (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify)) ∧
    ReleaseStep (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.A.length (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify)
      (.ok (releaseEff (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify) (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.A.length)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- Without such a derivation, the same arena is reset by both: the restricted `reset` holds. -/
theorem reset_alloc_ok : ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s arL := by decide

/-- The state `a6` of case 16 (`Ern.MM03`) is reached. -/
theorem a6_reachable : Reachable KA [] a6 := by
  have r0 : Reachable KA [] a0 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have r1 : Reachable KA [] a1 := .write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [1] a0 (.ok a1) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable KA [] a2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep KA 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)] a1 (.ok a2) from
      .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable KA [] a3 := .newArena (.write r2 (show Write3Step 0 [0] a2 (.ok a2w) from
    .ok (by decide))) (show NewArenaStep 3 3 a2w (.ok a3) from .ok (by decide))
  have r4 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) :=
    .derive r3 (show DeriveStep 0 0 .observe a3 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r5 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify) :=
    .derive r4 (show DeriveStep 2 2 .modify (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  exact .enter r5 (show EnterStep [4, 5] [(none, none, 0)] _ (.ok a6) from .ok (by decide))

/-- **`writeShared` branch** (brief, question 1, counterexample to keep): in `a6`, case 16 of the
kernel, the callee frame has only the `Observe` authority 4 on the arena value 0, whose leaf is
`SharedMutable` under `KA`, and no block is issued. The kernel `issue` of `[4]` into 6 and the kernel
`reset` are `ok` through the `writeShared` branch of `MetaRight`; `internal` 3 is exercisable at no
`Modify` (`MetaRightM` fails), so `derive` of `internal` on the region (place 4) or on the storage
(place 3), and `split` on the region, are rejected; the restricted operations are rejected too. -/
theorem ce_writeShared :
    Reachable KA [] a6 ∧ a6.arenas = [ar7] ∧ ar7.issued = [] ∧
    IssueAt KA 0 4 [4] 6 a6 (.ok a7) ∧ ResetAtStep KA 0 4 a6 (.ok (resetAtEff a6 0)) ∧
    ¬ MetaRightM a6 ar7 ∧
    DeriveStep 3 4 .modify a6 .reject ∧ SplitStep KA 3 [[4]] a6 .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 3 3 .modify a6 .reject ∧
    IssueR ar7 [4] 6 a6 .reject ∧ ¬ ResetPreR a6 ar7 :=
  ⟨a6_reachable, by decide, rfl,
    .ok (ar := ar7) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)),
    .ok (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide),
    .reject (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- **Two administrations** (`newArena_as_library`): the unguarded registration of `internal` 4 a
second time (`NewArenaPreNG` holds, the kernel guard rejects); the emission of `[5]` through entry 0
is `ok`; the emission of `[5]` through entry 1, whose metadata still has 5 available, is rejected by
the effective right (§77.5), as is `split` of `internal` on `[5]`: the kernel (I1) rejects the double
emission, and the metadata of entry 1 no longer separates `fail` from `reject`. -/
def sTwo : S3 := newArenaEff (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4

def sTwoIssued : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff sTwo arL [5] 2).1 0 (issueEff sTwo arL [5] 2).2

theorem ce_two_admins :
    NewArenaPreNG (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4 ∧ NewArenaStep 4 4 (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s .reject ∧
    ReachableNG K0 [] sTwoIssued ∧ sTwoIssued.arenas.map (·.available) = [[6], [5, 6]] ∧
    IssueAt K0 1 0 [5] 3 sTwoIssued .reject ∧ IssueStatic K0 sTwoIssued arL 0 [5] 3 ∧
    Avail arL [5] ∧ SplitStep K0 4 [[5]] sTwoIssued .reject := by
  have h1 : NewArenaPreNG (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4 := by decide
  have hr : ReachableNG K0 [] sTwo :=
    .newArenaNG (reachableNG_of_reachable (reach_run (by decide))) h1
  refine ⟨h1, .reject (by decide), .step hr (.issue (via := 0) (.ok (ar := arL) (by decide)
    (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)))), by decide,
    .reject (ar := arL) (by decide) (.noRight (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide,
    by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- **Inexact metadata with the guard**: in a reached state, a frame that can exercise `internal`
derives from it directly (`derive` of 4 on 5 at `Observe`); the region `[5]` is available in the
metadata and its emission is rejected by the effective right. The guard does not make the metadata
exact either. -/
def opsObs : List Op := opsAlloc ++ [.derive 4 5 .observe]

theorem ce_avail_reject :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsObs).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsObs).s.arenas = [arL] ∧
    IssueAt K0 0 0 [5] 2 (run K0 [] opsObs).s .reject ∧ IssueStatic K0 (run K0 [] opsObs).s arL 0 [5] 2 ∧
    Avail arL [5] :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide,
    .reject (ar := arL) (by decide) (.noRight (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide, by decide⟩

end Ern.Derived.Arena

/-- Arena invariant (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3; F1; F2). Clauses of §6: issued regions within the
administered storage (the footprint of `internal`); two simultaneously valid issued regions
disjoint; available regions disjoint from the still distributed ones; added: available regions
within the storage. Clause of A10: each emission is a `Modify` authority derived from `internal`
on its region. F2: the storage is a place of `P`, owned by anything (a local, a static, an
allocated root, a block): the ownership clause of A10 is removed. F1: `internal` is a `Modify`
authority held by a place, the arena value, and covers exactly the footprint of the storage. -/
def ArenaInv (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Prop :=
  (∀ l ∈ ar.available, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  ar.issued.Pairwise (fun e e' => s.Active e.2 → s.Active e'.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ e'.1) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, s.Active e.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ ar.available) ∧
  (∀ e ∈ ar.issued, ∃ y, s.A[e.2]? = some y ∧ y.origin = some ar.internal ∧
    y.footprint = e.1 ∧ y.mode = .modify) ∧
  ar.storage < s.P.length ∧
  (∃ (y : Authority) (v : Nat), s.A[ar.internal]? = some y ∧ y.mode = .modify ∧
    y.holder = .place v) ∧
  (∀ l, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P ar.storage)

/-- Right to update the metadata of the arena (A10; C6, aligned with `ProviderRight`): exercisable
`Modify` on the arena value, or an authority `via` exercisable at `Observe` (B2) with a present
effective mode on every metadata leaf, all `SharedMutable` (a `writeShared`, A9), with valid
dependencies. -/
def MetaRight (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (arenaValue s ar) (fun v => HasRight s .modify v) False ∨
  (s.ExercisableAt via .observe ∧ arenaValue s ar ≠ none ∧
    ∀ l ∈ metaLeaves s ar, effective s via l ≠ none ∧ k.SharedMutable l ∧ DepsValid s l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) :
    Decidable (MetaRight k s ar via) := by
  unfold MetaRight; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.issue(region)` (MM-03.3 §6; A10; J1): a `Modify` block derived from `internal`
on the region, held by the destination leaf; that leaf, and it only, becomes `Init` (J1, second
bullet), so the initialisation of the arena value is unchanged unless the destination is one of its
leaves (`issue_into_arena_value`; J1, third bullet: a question of the pass-8 report); the region
leaves `available` and joins `issued`. -/
def issueEff (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 × Arena :=
  ({ s.addAuth ⟨.modify, some ar.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩ with
      I := fun l => if l = dst then .init else s.I l },
   { ar with
      available := ar.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
      issued := (region, s.A.length) :: ar.issued })

/-- Static preconditions of `arena.issue(region)` (MM-03.3 §6; A10): metadata right (A10); the
region lies in the storage administered by `internal`; the destination `dst` of the block is
usable, exercisable in `Modify` (A2) and holds no initialised value; J1: `dst` is a leaf
(`isLeaf`) that holds no active authority. -/
def IssueStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Prop :=
  MetaRight k s ar via ∧ s.Active ar.internal ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧
  isLeaf s.P dst ∧
  ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst)
    True

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (via : Nat)
    (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Decidable (IssueStatic k s ar via region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStatic; infer_instance

/-- The region is available (MM-03.3 §6): otherwise `issue` fails (A10). -/
def Avail (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Prop := ∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ ar.available

instance (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (Avail ar region) := by
  unfold Avail; infer_instance

/-- The abstraction has, through `internal`, effective `Modify` on the region (MM-03.3 §6:
the abstraction has the authority needed to distribute the region). The
disjointness from active emissions is removed (A11): it follows from this right
(`issue_disjoint_redundant`). -/
def IssueRight (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ l ∈ region, effective s ar.internal l = some .modify

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (IssueRight s ar region) := by
  unfold IssueRight; infer_instance

/-- Outcomes of `issue` (A10): `ok`, defined failure `fail` with the state unchanged, `reject`
(pass-1 arbitrage 6). -/
inductive IOutcome where
  | ok (s : S3) (ar : Arena)
  | fail (s : S3) (ar : Arena)
  | reject

/-- `arena.issue` as a relation (MM-03.3 §6; A10): `reject` when a static precondition fails;
`fail`, with the state unchanged, when the region is unavailable; `reject` when the region is
available but `internal` lacks the right to distribute it; G4: `reject` when the arrival state,
where the block is held by `dst`, breaks `AnchorOrderHeld`; `ok` otherwise. A failed `issue`
creates no holding relation and has no arrival state, so G4 is not checked before `fail`. -/

/-- An arena entry (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3; F1): `storage` is the place of the administered storage;
`internal` is the authority that administers it, named by `newArena` (F1); `available` and
`issued` are the logical state of §6, `issued` mapping each issued region to the issued block.
The arena value is not a field: it is the place that holds `internal` (F1), which follows
transfers (A4). The anchor of §6 is not a field either: dependents anchor on the blocks (A10). -/
structure Arena where
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  available : List Nat
  issued : List (List Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq

/-- State `S3 = (F, P, I, A, D)` (MM-03.3 §1), without component `M` (pass-1 arbitrage 1).
`nF` is the next frame identity, so that an exited frame is never reused. `D q` lists the
anchors of place `q`, each an authority identity (pass-1 arbitrage 2). `dead q`: the place is
logically dead (A6, `endUse` and `free`); `freed q`: its storage was released by `free` (A6);
`pin l`: leaf `l` is dynamically pinned (A8). `arenas`: the arena entries registered by
`newArena` (D3). `callParams f`: the parameters given to frame `f` by `enterFrame`, a ghost record
(F6): set by `enterFrame`, never modified, read by no operation. -/
structure S3 where

/-- `newArena storage internal : ok | reject` as a relation (D3; F1). -/
def NewArenaStep (storage internal : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (NewArenaPre s storage internal) (newArenaEff s storage internal)

/-- `arena.issue` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the step `IssueStep` of the
recorded arena, whose new logical state is written back; a missing entry is rejected. An entry
whose `internal` is released is rejected by `IssueStatic`, which asks it active. -/
inductive IssueAt (k : K) (i via : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) :
    AOutcome → Prop where
  | ok {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.ok s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.ok (arenaSet s' i ar'))
  | fail {ar : Arena} {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar →
      IssueStep k ar via region dst s (.fail s' ar') → IssueAt k i via region dst s (.fail s)
  | reject {ar : Arena} : s.arenas[i]? = some ar → IssueStep k ar via region dst s .reject →
      IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject
  | none : s.arenas[i]? = none → IssueAt k i via region dst s .reject

/-- Preconditions of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` of the state (MM-03.3 §6; A10; D3): the entry
exists and is live (an entry whose `internal` is released cannot be reset), and `ResetPre`. -/
def ResetAtPre (k : K) (s : S3) (i via : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.arenas[i]?) (fun ar => s.Active ar.internal ∧ ResetPre k s ar via) False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable] (s : S3) (i via : Nat) :
    Decidable (ResetAtPre k s i via) := by
  unfold ResetAtPre; infer_instance

/-- Effect of `arena.reset()` on the entry `i` (D3): `resetEff`, the new logical state written
back. -/
def resetAtEff (s : S3) (i : Nat) : S3 :=
  match s.arenas[i]? with
  | some ar => arenaSet (resetEff s ar).1 i (resetEff s ar).2
  | none => s

/-- `arena.reset` on the entry `i` of the state as a relation (D3). -/

/-- Direction `issue` → sequence (brief, question 1): an `ok` of the restricted `issue` whose
destination is still exercisable at `Modify` in the arrival state is the `ok` of `split` of
`internal` on the region, then of `store` of the block into the destination, with the same
arrival state. The extra hypothesis is clause 5 of `store` (O8.5, `store_keeps_target_reachable`),
which the restricted `issue` does not check: `ce_g2` shows it is needed. Clause 3 of `store` on the
storage owned by the destination (O8.3) follows from clause 2 of `issue` (no active authority held
by the destination) in reached states (`ownedIn_holds`). -/
theorem issue_to_seq {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} (h : IssueR ar region dst s (.ok s' ar'))
    (hg2 : HasRight s' .modify dst) :
    SplitStep k ar.internal [region] s (.ok (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region))) ∧
      StoreStep s.A.length dst (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) (.ok s') := by
  obtain ⟨hwf, hinv, -, hais⟩ := reachable_invariants hdd hr
  have hrl := reachable_rootLive hdd hr
  obtain ⟨hst, -, hright, harr, he⟩ := issueR_ok_iff.1 h
  have hs' : s' = storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) s.A.length dst := by
    rw [← issueEffR_eq]; exact congrArg Prod.fst he
  subst hs'
  obtain ⟨hm, hact, hreg, hud, -, -, hleaf, hnoh, hnot⟩ := hst
  have hai := hais ar har hact
  have hex := (metaRightM_iff hai hact).1 hm
  obtain ⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩ := hact
  refine ⟨.ok ⟨⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩, hex, ?_, ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _, ?_⟩, .ok ?_⟩
  · intro r hr' p hp; rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp; exact hright p hp
  · intro r hr' p hp; rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp
    exact ⟨hreg p hp, by rw [hright p hp]; simp⟩
  · intro r hr' p hp j _ hd
    rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp
    unfold DistribExcl at hd
    cases hj : s.A[j]? with
    | none => rw [hj] at hd; exact hd
    | some y =>
      rw [hj] at hd; obtain ⟨ya, hanc, hpy, hmy⟩ := hd
      exact effective_ne_modify_of_desc hj ya hpy hanc hmy (hright p hp)
  · -- `StorePre` on the state after `split`
    have hy₀ : (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)).A[s.A.length]? = some (blockOf s ar region) :=
      addAuth_self _ _
    have hdl : dst < s.P.length := hud.lt
    have hfd : ∀ l, l ∈ footprint s.P dst ↔ l = dst := fun l => mem_footprint_leaf hleaf hdl
    have hu₁ : (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)).Usable dst :=
      (S3.Usable.congr (s := s) (s' := s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) rfl rfl rfl).2 hud
    have hne : (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)).effAnchor s.A.length ≠ s.A.length := by
      have := effAnchor_lt (s := s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) (x := s.A.length)
        (o := ar.internal) (by simp only [S3.org, hy₀]; rfl) (lt_of_getElem? hyi)
      omega
    refine ⟨by simp [OptP, blockOf, S3.top, S3.addAuth], hu₁, ?_, ?_, ?_, hleaf, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact hasRight_store_back hy₀ rfl hg2
    · intro l hl
      have hlr : l ∈ region := by simp only [S3.afp, hy₀] at hl; exact hl
      refine ⟨fun hld => hnot (by rw [(hfd l).1 hld] at hlr; exact hlr), fun q _ hown hlq => ?_⟩
      have hreg' : l ∈ yi.footprint := by simpa [S3.afp, hyi] using hreg l hlr
      have huq := usable_of_covered hinv.nd hyi yia hreg' hlq
      obtain ⟨j, z, hz, za, hzh⟩ := ownedIn_holds hwf hrl hleaf hown huq
      have := hnoh j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz))
      rw [hz] at this; exact this za hzh
    · rw [← effAnchorOK_store (p := dst) hy₀ hne]
      have h1 := harr.1
      rw [issueEffR_eq] at h1
      have hP : (storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) s.A.length dst).P =
          (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)).P := by rw [storeEff_eq hy₀]
      rwa [S3.pframe_congr hP] at h1
    · intro j hj
      by_cases hjl : j < s.A.length
      · rw [addAuth_lt hjl]
        exact hnoh j (List.mem_range.2 hjl)
      · have : j = s.A.length := by
          have := List.mem_range.1 hj; simp [S3.addAuth] at this; omega
        subst this; rw [hy₀]; simp [OptP, blockOf]
    · exact hg2
    · have h2 := harr.2; rw [issueEffR_eq] at h2; exact h2

/-- Direction sequence → `issue` (brief, question 1): an `ok` of `split` of `internal` on the
region, then of `store` of the block into the destination, on an available region whose destination
is not `Init`, is the `ok` of the restricted `issue`, with the same arrival state. The hypothesis on
`Init` is clause 2 of `issue` (§77.2), which `store` does not check (O8.2): `ce_init` shows it is
needed. The availability is the metadata of the arena: when it fails, `issue` fails (§77.4). -/
theorem seq_to_issue {s₁ s₂ : S3} (hsp : SplitStep k ar.internal [region] s (.ok s₁))
    (hst : StoreStep s.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂)) (hav : Avail ar region)
    (hni : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) :
    s₁ = s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region) ∧
      IssueR ar region dst s (.ok s₂ (issueEffR s ar region dst).2) := by
  obtain ⟨-, -, -, hais⟩ := reachable_invariants hdd hr
  obtain ⟨⟨hact, hex, hright, hreg, -, -⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
  obtain ⟨⟨-, hu₁, hrd₁, hcov, -, hleaf, hnoh₁, -, haoh⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hst
  rw [splitEff_one] at hu₁ hrd₁ hcov hleaf hnoh₁ haoh ⊢
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_⟩
  have hy₀ : (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)).A[s.A.length]? = some (blockOf s ar region) :=
    addAuth_self _ _
  have hud : s.Usable dst :=
    (S3.Usable.congr (s := s) (s' := s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) rfl rfl rfl).1 hu₁
  have hfd : ∀ l, l ∈ footprint s.P dst ↔ l = dst := fun l => mem_footprint_leaf hleaf hud.lt
  have hnot : dst ∉ region := by
    intro hd
    have := (hcov dst (by simp only [S3.afp, hy₀]; exact hd)).1
    exact this ((hfd dst).2 rfl)
  have hright' : IssueRight s ar region := fun l hl => hright region (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl
  have hai := hais ar har hact
  have harr' := issueEffR_eq s ar region dst
  have hstat : IssueStaticR s ar region dst := by
    refine ⟨(metaRightM_iff hai hact).2 hex, hact,
      fun l hl => (hreg region (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl).1, hud, ?_, hni, hleaf, ?_, hnot⟩
    · exact hasRight_addAuth_back hex (fun l hl => hright' l hl)
        (fun l hl hlr => hnot (by rw [(hfd l).1 hl] at hlr; exact hlr)) hrd₁
    · intro j hj
      have hjl := List.mem_range.1 hj
      have := hnoh₁ j (List.mem_range.2 (by simp only [S3.addAuth, List.length_append]; omega))
      rwa [addAuth_lt hjl] at this
  have harr : ArrivalR s ar region dst := by
    refine ⟨?_, by rw [harr']; exact haoh⟩
    rw [harr']
    have hP : (storeEff (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) s.A.length dst).P = s.P := by
      rw [storeEff_eq hy₀]; rfl
    refine haoh dst ((S3.Usable.congr hP (by rw [storeEff_eq hy₀]; rfl)
      (by rw [storeEff_eq hy₀]; rfl)).2 hud) s.A.length { blockOf s ar region with holder := .place dst }
      (by rw [storeEff_eq hy₀]; exact List.getElem?_set_self (by simp [S3.addAuth])) rfl rfl
  have hok := IssueR.ok hstat hav hright' harr
  rwa [harr'] at hok

/-- `issue_as_kernel` for a region (brief, question 1), in reached states: the restricted `issue`
is `ok` with a destination still exercisable at `Modify` iff the region is available, the
destination is not `Init`, and `split` of `internal` on the region then `store` of the block into
the destination are `ok`; the arrival state of the kernel part is the same, and the metadata is that
of the restricted `issue`. `fail` is `issueR_fail_iff`, `reject` is `issueR_reject_iff`. -/
theorem issue_as_kernel_split {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} :
    (IssueR ar region dst s (.ok s' ar') ∧ HasRight s' .modify dst) ↔
      Avail ar region ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧
      SplitStep k ar.internal [region] s (.ok (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region))) ∧
      StoreStep s.A.length dst (s.addAuth (blockOf s ar region)) (.ok s') ∧
      ar' = (issueEffR s ar region dst).2 := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨h, hg2⟩
    obtain ⟨hsp, hst⟩ := issue_to_seq hdd hr har h hg2
    obtain ⟨hstat, hav, -, -, he⟩ := issueR_ok_iff.1 h
    exact ⟨hav, hstat.2.2.2.2.2.1, hsp, hst, congrArg Prod.snd he⟩
  · rintro ⟨hav, hni, hsp, hst, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨-, h⟩ := seq_to_issue hdd hr har hsp hst hav hni
    exact ⟨h, (Guarded.ok_iff.1 hst).1.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1 |> fun h' => by
      rw [(Guarded.ok_iff.1 hst).2]; exact h'⟩

omit har in
/-- On a place `q` with a leaf, `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` (O1) is `split` of `internal` on
the footprint of `q` (O2, one region), with the same effect: the usability of `q` asked by
`derive` follows from `NoDangling`, `internal` being active and covering the footprint. -/
theorem derive_iff_split {q : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) {s₁ : S3} :
    DeriveStep ar.internal q .modify s (.ok s₁) ↔
      SplitStep k ar.internal [footprint s.P q] s (.ok s₁) := by
  obtain ⟨hwf, hinv, -, -⟩ := reachable_invariants hdd hr
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨⟨hact, hex, -, hsub, hal⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    have hm : ∀ p ∈ footprint s.P q, effective s ar.internal p = some .modify :=
      fun p hp => allows_modify_iff.1 (hal p hp)
    refine .ok ⟨hact, hex, ?_, ?_, List.pairwise_singleton _ _, ?_⟩
    · intro r hr' p hp; rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp; exact hm p hp
    · intro r hr' p hp; rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp
      exact ⟨hsub p hp, by rw [hm p hp]; simp⟩
    · intro r hr' p hp j _ hd
      rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hr'] at hp
      unfold DistribExcl at hd
      cases hj : s.A[j]? with
      | none => rw [hj] at hd; exact hd
      | some y =>
        rw [hj] at hd; obtain ⟨ya, hanc, hpy, hmy⟩ := hd
        exact effective_ne_modify_of_desc hj ya hpy hanc hmy (hm p hp)
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨⟨hact, hex, hright, hreg, -, -⟩, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hwf (s.P.length - q + 1) q (by omega) hq
    obtain ⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩ := hact
    have hli : l ∈ yi.footprint := by
      have := (hreg _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl).1; simpa [S3.afp, hyi] using this
    refine .ok ⟨⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩, hex, usable_of_covered hinv.nd hyi yia hli hl,
      fun p hp => (hreg _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) p hp).1,
      fun p hp => by rw [hright _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) p hp]; exact allows_some_modify _⟩

/-- `issue_as_kernel` (brief, question 1), with `derive` (O1) of `internal` at `Modify` on a place
`q`, the region being the footprint of `q`. Same statement as `issue_as_kernel_split`. A region that
is not the footprint of a place, the empty region included (`exists_mem_footprint`), is out of reach
of the kernel `derive`, which takes a place; `split` on one region covers it. -/
theorem issue_as_kernel {q : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) {s' : S3} {ar' : Arena} :
    (IssueR ar (footprint s.P q) dst s (.ok s' ar') ∧ HasRight s' .modify dst) ↔
      Avail ar (footprint s.P q) ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧
      DeriveStep ar.internal q .modify s (.ok (deriveEff s ar.internal q .modify)) ∧
      StoreStep s.A.length dst (deriveEff s ar.internal q .modify) (.ok s') ∧
      ar' = (issueEffR s ar (footprint s.P q) dst).2 := by
  rw [issue_as_kernel_split hdd hr har, derive_iff_split hdd hr hq, deriveEff_eq]

end IssueAsKernel

/-! ## Restricted `reset` (candidate Spec 1 §78) -/

/-- Preconditions of the restricted `reset` (candidate Spec 1 §78, with `MetaRightM`), as the
clauses of the kernel `ResetPre`: 1 restricted metadata right (§78.1); 2 no active authority
derived from `internal` (§78.2); 3 no usable place with an anchor in the subtree of origins of
`internal`, `internal` itself included, as the kernel reads §78.3. Transitive dependencies through
contained values are covered since every usable part is a usable place. -/
def ResetPreR (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Prop :=
  MetaRightM s ar ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ar.internal ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ s.Active j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, x ≠ ar.internal ∧ ar.internal ∉ s.ancs x)

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) : Decidable (ResetPreR s ar) := by
  unfold ResetPreR; infer_instance

/-- The restricted `reset` is the kernel `ResetPre` with the restricted right. -/
theorem resetPreR_iff {k : K} {via : Nat} {s : S3} {ar : Arena} :
    ResetPreR s ar ↔ MetaRightM s ar ∧ ResetPre k s ar via :=
  ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨h0, .inl h0, h1, h2⟩, fun ⟨h0, ⟨_, h1, h2⟩⟩ => ⟨h0, h1, h2⟩⟩

/-- The footprint of an authority derived, transitively, from `a` lies in the footprint of `a`
(I2, §42: "La création de droits dérivés n'accroît ni la portée"). -/
theorem afp_of_ancs {s : S3} (hwf : WF3 s) (h2 : I2 s) {a : Nat} :
    ∀ n j, j < n → a ∈ s.ancs j → ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ s.afp a
  | 0, _, h, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, j, hj, ha, l, hl => by
    cases hy : s.A[j]? with
    | none => simp [S3.afp, hy] at hl
    | some y =>
      have hly : l ∈ y.footprint := by simpa [S3.afp, hy] using hl
      cases ho : y.origin with
      | none =>
        have : s.org j = none := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
        rw [S3.ancs, chain_none this] at ha; simp at ha
      | some o =>
        have hoj := hwf.origin j y o hy ho
        obtain ⟨x, hx, hfx⟩ := h2 j y o hy ho
        have hlo : l ∈ s.afp o := by simp only [S3.afp, hx]; exact (hfx l hly).1
        have horg : s.org j = some o := by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]
        rw [S3.ancs, chain_cons horg hoj] at ha
        rcases List.mem_cons.1 ha with rfl | ha
        · exact hlo
        · exact afp_of_ancs hwf h2 n o (by omega) ha l hlo

## 46. Arènes comme états d’administration

Chaque entrée possède les champs suivants :

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Region>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

L'arène est **vivante** si `internal` est active. La **valeur arène** est l'emplacement détenteur de `internal`, distinct du propriétaire éventuel de `storage`. Le stockage administré peut être local, statique, alloué ou issu d'une autre arène, sous les préconditions de `newArena` et les invariants applicables. `available` et `issued` restent bien **dans l'entrée d'arène**.

## 47. État initial

L'état initial comporte le seul cadre de base 0 et le stockage statique déclaré. Chaque feuille statique a son état initial `Init` ou `Uninit` tel que déclaré. Les racines des emplacements statiques directement possédés par le cadre 0 ont une autorité racine `Modify` détenue par ce cadre ; un statique peut aussi être possédé par un autre statique, sa racine étant alors détenue par celui-ci. L'état initial n'invente ni allocation dynamique, ni autorité dérivée, ni ancre implicite, ni arène. Le cadre initial ne sort pas.

## 48. Contrat paramétrique externe

`K` contient les prédicats `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat` et `Satisfiable`. Leurs obligations sont fixées à la section 80. `K` ne peut ni fabriquer des droits d’accès, ni supprimer une obligation de la Charte. Le prédicat `Invalidates` ne fait pas partie du présent contrat.

# VII. Invariants des états atteignables

Les états de la machine sont soumis à des exigences structurelles, de validité et d’exclusivité qui sont préservées par les transitions autorisées sous leurs contrats externes déclarés.
-------
## 55. ArenaInv — Invariants des arènes

Pour chaque arène vivante :

- `storage` désigne un emplacement existant et utilisable ; l'empreinte de `internal` est exactement celle de `storage` ;
- `internal` est active, de mode propre `Modify`, détenue par la valeur arène ;
- les régions disponibles et les régions émises appartiennent au stockage administré ;
- deux émissions encore actives ont des régions disjointes ; une région encore émise n'appartient pas simultanément aux régions disponibles ;
- chaque autorité de bloc encore émis est une dérivée de `internal` conforme aux règles d'exclusivité et de validité ;
- les restrictions d'ancrage et de possession sont respectées.

Les entrées d'arène ne constituent pas, à elles seules, un propriétaire supplémentaire de stockage. Deux arènes vivantes peuvent couvrir des feuilles communes lorsque leurs autorités `internal` sont distinctes et que leurs droits effectifs sont compatibles ; aucune disjonction **globale** des empreintes d'arènes n'est imposée.

## 56. Unicité de l’administration vivante

**Une identité d’autorité peut être `internal` d’au plus une abstraction d’administration vivante**, qu’il s’agisse d’une entrée d’arène ou d’une instance d’administration de bibliothèque (notamment `HandlePool`). Avant d’inscrire une nouvelle abstraction, `newArena` et toute opération analogue de bibliothèque doivent vérifier conjointement l’absence de cette identité dans **les deux registres des abstractions vivantes**. L’unicité porte sur l’identité de l’autorité `internal`, non sur la seule intersection éventuelle des empreintes : des abstractions ayant des `internal` distincts ne sont pas interdites du seul fait que leurs empreintes se chevauchent. Les contrats de bibliothèque doivent mettre les informations nécessaires à cette garde à disposition de l’opération de création ; il ne suffit pas de contrôler son propre registre isolément.

Cette garde n’ajoute ni une permission ni une allocation, et n’introduit pas un mécanisme général de détection des cycles d’autorités. La représentation physique et l’encapsulation des registres des bibliothèques restent extérieures à ce noyau.

## 57. Invariant principal

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

Sur les états atteints depuis `S3.init statics` sous `DDSound(K)`, le noyau garantit :

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan \land
\bigwedge_{ar\text{ vivante}} ArenaInv(ar)
\]

I5, lié au stockage épinglé, reste une **obligation spécialisée** de `K.Pinned`, et non une clause automatiquement déduite des seuls accès séquentiels. Cette propriété est exigée des états atteints sous les hypothèses déclarées. Sa correspondance avec les allocations et les octets exige le raffinement défini ci-dessous.

# VIII. Définition des transitions et gestion des autorités

Les opérations ci-dessous sont des règles de transition abstraites. Elles distinguent un rejet de la discipline, un échec défini et une transition admise.

## 58. Issues des transitions

Toute opération a une issue conceptuelle parmi :

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` signifie que la discipline statique n'autorise pas le pas ; ce n'est ni un trap runtime implicite, ni un `ub` de la machine mémoire élémentaire. `fail` est un **échec défini**, laissant l'état inchangé ; seules `alloc` et `issue` peuvent l'émettre dans ce noyau. Pour toutes les autres opérations, l'issue est `ok` ou `reject`. Pour `alloc` et `issue`, le contrôle des préconditions statiques précède la détermination de l'échec dynamique, sauf les précisions d'ordre de contrôle indiquées dans leurs règles.

Une transition `ok` doit respecter ses préconditions, appliquer exactement ses effets prescrits et conserver les invariants pertinents. Aucune transition ne fabrique une permission pour rendre sa conclusion vraie. Les changements de détention et d'ancres s'évaluent sur l'**état d'arrivée** lorsqu'une règle le prévoit explicitement.

## 59. Conservation implicite des modes et ancres

Les changements d'autorité effective sont **dérivés** des autorités actives et de leurs origines ; aucune mutation d'un indicateur `Suspended` n'est effectuée. Les opérations d'accès ne changent pas une ancre sans effet de transfert, de `depend`, de `store`, de libération ou de ré-ancrage explicitement autorisé. Les feuilles qui deviennent `Init` proviennent d'une écriture admise (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, `issue`) ou d'un transfert depuis une feuille source déjà `Init` et correspondante ; les feuilles initialisées dans `S3.init` sont déclarées comme telles.

## 60. O1 — Dérivation d’une autorité

**Préconditions**

1. `source` est une autorité dérivée ou racine active, `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` est vrai ; sa chaîne d'origines et ses ancres sont valides.
2. Les feuilles de `region` existent et appartiennent à l'empreinte de `source` ; `mode` n'excède pas le droit effectif disponible sur ces feuilles.
3. L'ajout conserve l'exclusivité I1 : aucune autorité active non apparentée ne devient incompatible avec le droit dérivé, et les descendants déjà actifs sont respectés.
4. Le nouveau cadre détenteur est le cadre courant, vivant. Les restrictions d'empreinte et d'ancrage de l'état admissible restent vraies.
-----
# XIV. Arènes et invalidations collectives

L’arène est une instance du noyau d’accès et de possession, pas une seconde machine de permissions indépendante.

## 76. O17 — Création d’une arène administrée

**Préconditions**

1. `storage` est un emplacement existant, utilisable, sous `Modify` exerçable par le cadre courant. Il peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène précédente.
2. `internal` est nommée explicitement par l'appelant, existe, est active, de mode propre `Modify` et `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` est vrai.
3. `internal` est **détenue par un emplacement** : cet emplacement est la valeur arène ; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Garde d’administration unifiée (section 56) :** aucune abstraction d’administration **vivante**, qu’elle soit une arène ou une instance de bibliothèque telle qu’un pool de handles, n’utilise déjà cette identité `internal`. Les registres d’arènes **et** des instances de bibliothèque sont consultés avant l’inscription. Deux identités distinctes peuvent couvrir des feuilles communes : ce n’est pas en soi une cause de rejet.
5. Toutes les feuilles de la valeur arène qui détient `internal` sont déjà `Init` ; la construction ne les initialise pas implicitement.
6. Les relations de dépendance, de détenteur, de stockage et d'administration respectent `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld` et les invariants d'arène attendus.

**Effet `ok`** : ajout d'une entrée vivante `{storage, internal, available, issued}` ; l'ensemble `available` initial représente le stockage administré, `issued` est initialement vide. Aucun emplacement, droit d'accès ou état `Init` n'est fabriqué par l'inscription de l'entrée. **Autre issue :** `reject`.

L'identité de `internal` et non l'indice de `storage` est la clé de non-duplication des arènes vivantes. Il n'existe pas de contrainte globale imposant que des arènes vivantes aient des empreintes deux à deux disjointes.

## 77. O18 — Émission d’un bloc d’arène

**Préconditions statiques**

1. L'entrée `arena` existe et est vivante ; `internal` est active. La valeur arène peut être légalement administrée (`MetaRight`).
2. `region` appartient au stockage administré ; `destination` est une **feuille** utilisable, non `Init` (elle peut notamment être `Uninit` ou `Moved`), ne détenant aucune autorité active ; la destination peut légalement recevoir la valeur du bloc au mode `Modify`.
   **Prévention locale de l’auto-blocage : la feuille `destination` n’appartient pas à `region`, y compris lorsque la région est déclarée disponible.** Cette condition est statique et est vérifiée avant le `fail` de disponibilité.
3. Les restrictions **statiques** de validité et de non-échappement applicables à la destination sont satisfaites. Le contrôle de `AnchorOrder` qui dépend de la nouvelle ancre est effectué sur **l’état d’arrivée simulé**, après la vérification de disponibilité décrite au point 4 ; il ne peut transformer une émission indisponible (`fail`) en `reject`.

**Contrôle de disponibilité et d'exercice**

4. Si les conditions statiques tiennent mais que `region` n'appartient plus à `available`, l'opération produit **`fail` et laisse tout l'état inchangé**. Une région indisponible n'autorise pas à contourner un rejet statique préalable.
5. Si la région est disponible, le mode effectif de `internal` sur cette région doit permettre `Modify` ; à défaut, l'issue est `reject`. La région ne peut chevaucher une région émise encore active.
6. Le résultat simulé doit respecter `AnchorOrderHeld` **dans l'état d'arrivée** ; une émission vers une valeur plus durable qu'une ancre locale ne devient pas valide du seul fait qu'elle est stockée chez l'appelant.

**Effet `ok`** : une autorité de bloc d'identité fraîche, dérivée de `internal` et de mode `Modify`, est émise pour la région ; elle est détenue par `destination`, qui reçoit l'ancre correspondante. La région quitte `available` et est ajoutée à `issued` avec son autorité. **Seule la feuille `destination` passe à `Init`** ; aucune autre feuille de la valeur arène ne change d'initialisation. Les émissions antérieures restent intactes et valides. Une émission n'installe pas automatiquement des ancres sur des valeurs tierces : celles-ci doivent utiliser leurs mécanismes légaux de dépendance.

**Issues :** `ok`, `fail` (région indisponible après validation statique), `reject` (règle statique, droit effectif ou ancrage non respecté). La destination peut être une feuille de la valeur arène elle-même : son initialisation constitue alors **l'écriture explicite de cette destination**, et non une initialisation implicite des métadonnées de toute la valeur arène.

## 78. O19 — Réinitialisation collective d’arène

**Préconditions**

1. L’entrée existe et est vivante. La mise à jour des métadonnées de l’arène est autorisée par **`MetaRight(s,arena)`** : `Modify` exerçable sur la valeur arène **ou** mutation `writeShared` légale sur ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. L’autorité `internal` et les autres restrictions de l’arène restent valides.
2. Aucune autorité dérivée de `internal` ne reste active : aucune émission vivante ni dérivée subsistante ne peut être invalidée par ce `reset`.
3. Aucun emplacement encore utilisable ne dépend, directement ou transitivement, d'une ancre située dans le sous-arbre d'origines de `internal`. Les obligations de validité d'autres arènes imbriquées restent satisfaites.

**Effet `ok`** : la totalité des régions du stockage administré redevient disponible et la liste des émissions est vidée, sous le contrat de l'arène. Les anciennes autorités émises ne peuvent plus être utilisées, car les préconditions excluaient leur activité. **Aucune feuille n'est rendue `Init` par `reset`**, y compris dans la valeur arène. **Autre issue :** `reject`.

La réutilisation sûre après `reset` exige que les anciennes émissions et leurs dépendants actifs aient effectivement cessé d'exister. Une région historiquement émise ne reste pas définitivement indisponible pour cette seule raison.

# XV. Dépendances transitives, sorties et comportement des valeurs

Les valeurs dépendantes peuvent survivre à des transferts et à des appels seulement si les ancres et droits nécessaires restent valides. L’accès de seconde classe n’implique pas une référence persistante arbitraire.

## 79. Valeurs non échappantes et retours

La seconde classe des autorités d'accès n'interdit pas de construire une valeur portant une autorité dérivée, ni de restituer un résultat dépendant d'une ressource appartenant à l'appelant. Ce qui est interdit est de prolonger artificiellement la validité d'une origine locale.

Un scénario typique est :

```text
arena = create_arena()
buffer = create_buffer(arena)
use(buffer)
endUse(buffer)       // ou libération équivalente de ses droits dépendants
arena.reset()
```

Le scénario est admissible lorsque :

1. l'appel reçoit et exerce des autorités valides sur l'arène ;
2. une émission fournit un bloc disjoint des émissions vivantes ;
3. la valeur résultat est ancrée sur les droits réellement nécessaires ;
4. son transfert vers l'appelant respecte `SameShape`, les détenteurs, `AnchorOrder` et `AnchorOrderHeld` ;
5. `exitFrame` peut ré-ancrer les autorités survivantes sans utiliser une racine locale morte ;
6. `reset` est refusé tant que le résultat dépendant ou une autorité de bloc reste active, puis redevient admissible après la fin effective de ces droits.

Une valeur « non échappante » n'est donc pas nécessairement limitée à son cadre de création. Elle peut survivre à une fonction lorsqu'elle dépend d'une ancre de l'appelant, sans qu'un stockage local mort soit prolongé. Ce résultat n'implique **pas** la protection forte de toutes les autorités d'un paramètre durant toute l'invocation : l'interprétation historique des ré-emprunts et cette propriété sont différées à la Spec 3.

Les propriétés de transfert entre threads et de partageabilité ne se déduisent pas du seul présent modèle séquentiel. Elles dépendront des ressources externes, des autorités contenues, des ancres, des restrictions de confinement et du modèle de concurrence de la Spec 2.
